declaration.preface:
Shilpa Medicare Ltd (Group) recognizes that delivering affordable, life-saving medicines to patients around the world requires not only technical excellence within its own operations, but responsible, transparent, and sustainable practices throughout its supply chain. The raw materials, chemicals, solvents, packaging, laboratory consumables, equipment, and services that enter SML's manufacturing processes carry environmental, social, and ethical implications that extend well beyond our factory gates.

This Responsible Supplier Engagement Policy formalizes SML's commitment to integrating environmental sustainability, social responsibility, ethical governance, and procurement excellence into every sourcing decision. It establishes clear expectations for our procurement teams and for the suppliers, contractors, vendors, and service providers forming part of SML's extended value chain - building a supply chain that is not only cost-effective and quality-assured, but also environmentally responsible, socially fair, and governed with integrity.
declaration.declaration:
The objectives of this Responsible Supplier Engagement Policy of Shilpa Medicare Limited are to:

Embed environmental sustainability criteria including GHG emissions, energy efficiency, water conservation, waste minimization, chemical safety, and biodiversity protection into supplier qualification, evaluation, and selection across all procurement categories.

Ensure all suppliers, contractors, and service providers uphold fair, safe, and lawful labor standards including prohibition of child and forced labor, fair wages, safe conditions, and non-discrimination aligned with ILO Core Conventions.

Establish a risk-based supplier due diligence and monitoring program that identifies, assesses, and mitigates environmental, social, ethical, and supply security risks across SML's key procurement categories.

Promote sustainable materials, green chemistry inputs, eco-designed packaging, and low-carbon logistics solutions across SML's supply chain, supporting SML's environmental responsibility and decarbonization goals.

Drive continuous improvement through supplier engagement, capacity building, collaborative goal-setting, and transparent performance reporting, aligned with the PSCI Code of Conduct.

Maintain full compliance with all applicable procurement-related laws and international standards, including anti-corruption, anti-slavery, responsible sourcing, and customs compliance requirements.

Deliver procurement excellence - quality, cost, reliability, and innovation - without compromising sustainability, ethics, or compliance, building a resilient and responsible supply chain.
declaration.scope:
This Policy applies to all operations of Shilpa Medicare Limited and its group entities, Subsidiaries, Joint Ventures including API manufacturing facilities, formulation plants, R&D centers, CDMO operations, biologics units, corporate and administrative offices, and all associated with Shilpa Medicare Operational Locations. The Policy also extends to all global sales offices located in Malaysia, Austria, Dubai (UAE), the United Kingdom, Spain, and the United States of America.

It is applicable to all employees (permanent and contract), management, directors, business associates, vendors, contractors, and all internal and external stake holders working on behalf of the Company.

Supplier Environmental Practices: We assess the environmental performance of all new and existing strategic suppliers across key categories - APIs, chemical raw materials, solvents, excipients, packaging, and logistics - using structured environmental questionnaires, and third-party audit reports as appropriate.
We ensure that all procurement and purchase department personnel are regularly trained on environmental issues associated with procurement.

We will prioritize suppliers who demonstrate robust environmental management systems (ISO 14001 certification or equivalent), effective GHG emissions tracking, water conservation initiatives, and responsible chemical and waste management aligned with applicable regulatory standards.

We will engage key API, chemical, and solvent suppliers in collaborative programs to reduce carbon intensity, solvent usage, and waste generation associated with critical raw materials, supporting SML's Scope 3 emission reduction goals.

We will give sourcing preference - all quality and regulatory factors being equal - to suppliers offering greener synthesis routes, reduced-solvent processes, bio-based inputs, recyclable packaging, and low-carbon logistics options.

We will work with packaging material suppliers to transition SML's secondary and tertiary packaging to recyclable, reduced-material, or biodegradable alternatives, in line with SML's Environmental Responsibility Policy.
Supplier Social & Labor Practices: We will require all direct material suppliers and key service providers to commit to the labor rights, occupational health and safety, environmental responsibility, ethics, and management systems as a condition of qualifying as an approved SML supplier.
We ensure that all procurement and purchase department personnel are regularly trained on social issues associated with procurement.

We conduct social and labor compliance due diligence on all new strategic suppliers before approval, using self-assessment questionnaires, social audit reports (SMETA, SA8000, or equivalent), and third-party verification appropriate to supplier risk profile.

We maintain absolute zero tolerance for child labor, forced labor, bonded labor, debt bondage, or human trafficking in any tier of SML's supply chain. Suppliers must provide age verification documentation and declare compliance with applicable anti-slavery laws.
We prioritize and progressively increase business with suppliers holding ISO 45001 certification or equivalent, subject to quality and regulatory compliance.

We will expect all suppliers to provide safe and healthy working conditions in compliance with applicable national OHS laws including PPE provision, documented risk assessments, emergency response plans, and health surveillance where required.

We engage high-risk suppliers through structured improvement programs, targeted social audits, and collaborative capacity-building initiatives to drive measurable labor practice improvements over time.
Sustainable Procurement Goals: We will integrate sustainability performance as a weighted evaluation criterion alongside quality, price, reliability, and regulatory compliance in all strategic supplier selections, RFPs, and contract renewals across critical procurement categories.

We will develop a Preferred Supplier Program that recognizes and rewards suppliers demonstrating leadership in sustainability, continuous improvement, verified labor and environmental compliance, and active collaboration on SML's sustainability goals.

We develop category-specific sustainable procurement strategies for SML's highest-impact sourcing categories - oncology APIs, hazardous solvents, packaging materials, laboratory consumables, and freight - incorporating sustainability targets and preferred supplier criteria.

We promote supplier diversity by providing equitable access to SML's supply base for SMEs, women-owned businesses, local suppliers, and socially disadvantaged enterprises where quality, regulatory, and business requirements are met.
We are collaborating with industry associations and sustainability frameworks - PSCI, UNGC, and Supply Chain - to share best practices and drive industry-wide sustainable procurement improvement.
Governance Goals: We maintain a robust Supplier Code of Conduct aligned with PSCI, ILO Core Conventions, and SML's Business Ethics Policy that all approved suppliers must formally acknowledge as a contractual condition of doing business with SML.

We conduct risk-based procurement ethics due diligence on all new suppliers and existing suppliers at periodic intervals, covering anti-corruption compliance, beneficial ownership transparency, sanctions screening, and regulatory standing.

We will enforce strict conflict-of-interest standards in all procurement decisions - procurement team members must complete annual COI Declarations, recuse themselves from decisions involving related parties, and report concerns to Compliance immediately.

We will embed sustainability and ethics requirements into all supplier contracts including anti-corruption, anti-slavery, environmental compliance, labor standards, audit access, and data protection clauses ensuring obligations are legally binding and enforceable.

We conduct risk-based supplier on-site audits and assessments covering environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria to evaluate compliance, identify gaps, and drive continuous improvement across the supply chain

responsibilities.duty: Approve and endorse the Responsible Supplier Engagement Policy and ensure it is integrated into SML's sustainability strategy, business objectives, and corporate governance framework.
Provide visible leadership commitment to responsible sourcing, supply chain sustainability, and ethical procurement across all SML entities.
Ensure adequate financial, human, and technological resources are allocated for effective Policy implementation, supplier engagement, and performance monitoring.
Translate the Policy into actionable programs, annual targets, and category-level initiatives across all SML procurement functions.
Review supply chain sustainability performance, progress against quantitative targets, and emerging supply chain risks on a quarterly basis.
Ensure sustainability and ethics considerations are integrated into capital expenditure, new supplier approvals, strategic partnerships, and CDMO onboarding decisions.
Review Policy Regularly
Own Policy implementation across all SML procurement entities, ensuring sustainability and ethics criteria are embedded in all sourcing processes, category strategies, and contract frameworks.
Lead the Preferred Supplier Program, Supplier Code of Conduct enforcement, COI management, and sustainable procurement performance reporting.
Monitor and report procurement sustainability KPIs - supplier assessment coverage, spend under sustainability evaluation, audit outcomes - to Senior Management quarterly.
Provide technical guidance on supplier environmental assessment criteria, GHG reporting methodology, packaging sustainability, and Scope 3 quantification.
Collaborate with Procurement on supplier environmental audits, and supply chain emissions data collection.
Track and report supply chain environmental performance metrics - Scope 3, packaging sustainability, supplier environmental audit findings - in the annual BRSR.
Execute sustainable procurement at operational level: supplier qualification, sustainability questionnaires, due diligence, RFP sustainability scoring, and contract compliance monitoring.
Maintain the Approved Vendor List and Preferred Supplier List, ensuring currency, accuracy, and compliance with qualification and renewal criteria.
Report supplier non-compliances, audit findings, and procurement ethics concerns to the Procurement Head and Compliance team without delay.
Review and approve supplier contract templates ensuring mandatory sustainability, ethics, anti-corruption, anti-slavery, and audit access clauses are correctly drafted and legally enforceable.
Conduct anti-corruption, sanctions, and ethics screening for new suppliers as part of the procurement due diligence process.
Investigate any reported procurement ethics violations, conflicts of interest, or supplier misconduct allegations.
Comply with this Policy and all related procurement procedures, codes of conduct, and training requirements at all times.
Apply sustainability, ethics, and governance criteria in all supplier interactions, sourcing decisions, and commercial negotiations.

policy.monitoring:
Shilpa Medicare Limited is committed to the continuous improvement of its sustainable procurement performance across all sourcing categories and supplier relationships. Sustainability considerations are embedded into the full procurement lifecycle from supplier identification and qualification through contract award, onboarding, monitoring, and renewal.

Supplier sustainability scores, audit findings, CAPA status, spend under assessed suppliers, social compliance declarations, and packaging sustainability metrics tracked at category and entity level on a regular basis.

Periodic internal procurement compliance audits and independent supply chain sustainability assessments evaluate adherence to Policy requirements, identify gaps, and verify progress against targets.

All supplier non-compliances, audit findings, social or environmental supply chain incidents, and procurement ethics concerns are reported, root-cause analyzed, and resolved through the CAPA system within defined timelines.

Sustainable procurement performance covering all four issue areas is reviewed by the Procurement Head, EHS & Sustainability Head, and Senior Management quarterly.

Shilpa Medicare Limited maintains a structured and transparent process to monitor and report sustainable procurement performance across all operations. Key data on supplier sustainability scores, social audit outcomes, CAPA status, spend under sustainability-evaluated suppliers, packaging sustainability metrics, Scope 3 supply chain emissions, procurement ethics compliance, and COI declaration completion are systematically collected, validated, and reviewed quarterly at corporate level and annually for external disclosure.

Annual sustainable procurement data is disclosed in SML's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) filed with BSE and NSE under SEBI LODR Regulations, and in SML's periodic self-assessment, aligned with GRI Standards and the PSCI framework.
policy.reviewMechanism: This Responsible Supplier Engagement Policy is reviewed at least once every year, or whenever triggered by significant changes in business operations, applicable laws or regulations, material supply chain incidents, or significant stakeholder concerns. The review is conducted by the Procurement Head in consultation with the EHS & Sustainability Head, the Legal team, and Senior Management.
